title: Service Operations Skill Tree
subtitle: A navigable operating model from arrivals and capacity to quality and fulfilled demand
provenance: All values are synthetic planning assumptions supplied by this template; no empirical performance claim is implied.

modules.question: Which capabilities turn incoming demand into completed work?
modules.claim: Demand and capacity meet at the service gate, then first-pass yield determines completed work.
modules.selectionRationale: A qualitative skill tree makes the prerequisite structure explicit while binding every recurring operating value once.
modules.rejectedAlternative: A dashboard card was rejected because it would hide the prerequisite and merge structure.

modules.question: What are the exact intake and service quantities?
modules.claim: The ledger distinguishes demand, capacity, served demand, and unserved demand without implying extra arithmetic.
modules.selectionRationale: A table provides an exact numerical cross-check for quantities echoed across the world.
modules.rejectedAlternative: A pie chart was rejected because capacity is a constraint, not a disjoint part of demand.

modules.question: How large is incoming demand relative to available capacity?
modules.claim: One shared zero baseline reveals whether capacity stands above or below incoming demand.
modules.selectionRationale: Shared-scale bars support a direct magnitude comparison in the same unit.
modules.rejectedAlternative: Independent gauges were rejected because they would conceal the common scale.

modules.question: Does demand cross the available-capacity threshold?
modules.claim: The load ratio crosses 100 percent exactly when demand exceeds capacity.
modules.selectionRationale: A bullet chart preserves values above 100 percent and makes the capacity threshold explicit.
modules.rejectedAlternative: A radial utilization gauge was rejected because legal overload can exceed 100 percent.

modules.question: What is the signed difference between capacity and demand?
modules.claim: A positive gap is headroom, while a negative gap is an explicit capacity deficit.
modules.selectionRationale: A table retains the signed value honestly without forcing it onto an unsupported diverging bar.
modules.rejectedAlternative: A comparative bar was rejected because the legal capacity-gap domain crosses zero.

modules.question: How do demand and capacity determine served and unserved work?
modules.claim: The bottleneck takes the minimum as served demand and exposes only the positive excess as unserved demand.
modules.selectionRationale: A dependency network displays both direct parents for each bottleneck outcome.
modules.rejectedAlternative: A flow diagram was rejected because capacity is a constraint rather than a conserved branch of demand.

modules.question: What bounded share of served work succeeds on its first attempt?
modules.claim: First-pass yield stays within zero and one across the full legal domain.
modules.selectionRationale: A radial gauge is truthful for one bounded fraction with a meaningful perfect-yield endpoint.
modules.rejectedAlternative: A line chart was rejected because the brief contains scenarios rather than a sampled time series.

modules.question: Where does every served item go after its first attempt?
modules.claim: Served work is conserved exactly as completed work plus rework in every legal state.
modules.selectionRationale: A conserved flow is justified because completed and rework rates are mutually exclusive branches whose algebraic sum equals served rate.
modules.rejectedAlternative: Independent bars were rejected because they would hide the shared conserved source.

modules.question: How far apart are first-pass completions and rework volume?
modules.claim: Completed and rework rates share one zero baseline and one items-per-hour scale.
modules.selectionRationale: Shared-scale bars make the magnitude gap between the two disjoint outcomes immediately legible.
modules.rejectedAlternative: Another flow was rejected because this module asks for magnitude comparison rather than routing.

modules.question: What share of all incoming demand completes on the first pass?
modules.claim: The fulfilled share combines the capacity bottleneck with first-pass quality and remains bounded by 100 percent.
modules.selectionRationale: A bounded gauge summarizes the end-to-end share without hiding its exact readout.
modules.rejectedAlternative: A load bullet was rejected because this ratio cannot exceed 100 percent.

modules.question: How does unserved demand reconcile incoming demand to served demand?
modules.claim: Incoming demand minus nonnegative unserved demand equals served demand in every legal state.
modules.selectionRationale: A waterfall makes the exact opening-minus-deduction-equals-ending identity visible.
modules.rejectedAlternative: A stack was rejected because the explanatory task is ordered reconciliation rather than part composition.

modules.question: What are the magnitudes of completed, rework, and unserved outcomes?
modules.claim: Three disjoint outcome rates are compared on one shared items-per-hour scale.
modules.selectionRationale: Shared-scale bars compare outcome magnitudes without implying that constraints are flow branches.
modules.rejectedAlternative: A second Sankey was rejected because unserved demand never enters the served-work disposition flow.
